name: Evercore Inc.
reason: Advisory earnings are driven by M&A/capital-markets activity (EPS fell 46% in 2023, margin swung 15-34%), so they cannot be forecast with confidence.

name: Vistance Networks, Inc.
reason: Shrinking business (revenue CAGR -6.6%, EPS 0.29x 10y peak) with net debt/EBITDA of 29x and negative 10y avg ROIC.

name: PROG Holdings, Inc.
reason: Lease-to-own lender to subprime consumers with revenue CAGR -2.7%; earnings depend on credit losses and regulation, and it is cheap but not special.

name: Western Midstream Partners, LP
reason: Midstream G&P tied to Permian volumes and one dominant customer (Occidental), with net debt/EBITDA 3.55x and units rising 5.9%/yr.

name: Sprouts Farmers Market, Inc.
reason: Healthy-grocery format with clear secular demand and ~10% unit growth, EPS CAGR 20% with shares down 4.5%/yr and low leverage (1.7x); main risk is the 7.8% EBIT margin at a 10y high.

name: Altria Group, Inc.
reason: Cigarette volumes are in secular decline (revenue CAGR 0.7%) with litigation/regulatory risk and consensus EPS growth of only ~4%; 74.9% margin includes one-offs (adj/GAAP gap 63%).

name: Morgan Stanley Direct Lending Fund
reason: Middle-market BDC whose earnings follow rate and credit cycles (EPS 0.45x peak, consensus -9.7% FY1), with 7.7x leverage and no specialness.

name: SS&C Technologies Holdings, Inc.
reason: Growth has come from acquisitions (acq/FCF 1.18x, shares +2.9%/yr) with 10y avg ROIC of 4.7% and a large adjusted/GAAP gap (85%).

name: Delek US Holdings, Inc.
reason: Refiner whose earnings swing with crack spreads (losses in 4 of 11 years, 10y avg EBIT margin 1.0%), now at 1.0x 10y peak EPS.

name: Matson, Inc.
reason: Earnings are set by trans-Pacific freight rates (EPS went 4.4 to 27.1 to 8.3 over 2020-23); the Jones Act franchise is stable but too small to drive growth.

name: First American Financial Corp.
reason: Title insurance earnings are tied to mortgage rates and housing turnover (EPS fell 78% in 2022 and stays 0.54x peak).

name: Genpact Ltd.
reason: Steady record (EPS growth >=7% in 9/10 years, 0.65x leverage), but AI automation is a credible 5-year threat to labor-based BPO pricing.

name: Crocs, Inc.
reason: Very profitable (ROIC 27%), but a single fashion-driven clog brand plus a struggling HEYDUDE acquisition make 5-10 year demand impossible to forecast; consensus FY3 growth is 1.8%.

name: Lazard, Inc.
reason: Advisory and asset management earnings depend on capital markets (EPS 0.48x 10y peak, 10y EPS CAGR -3.8%).

name: General Motors Co.
reason: Cyclical, capital-heavy auto OEM with EV/tariff disruption, net debt/EBITDA 6.8x including GM Financial, and negative FCF conversion.

name: Eagle Materials, Inc.
reason: Low-cost cement/wallboard producer with good capital allocation, but EPS is 0.97x its 10y peak after a big 2021-23 price run-up in a housing-cyclical business (consensus FY1 -13%).

name: CarMax, Inc.
reason: EBIT margin fell from 6.7% to 2.2% amid online used-car competition and auto-credit exposure (EPS 0.42x peak), with on-balance-sheet auto finance debt.

name: Keurig Dr Pepper, Inc.
reason: Recently transformed by the JDE Peet's deal and planned split, with leverage at 3.9x and share count up 21.6%/yr from mergers, so the future shape is unclear.

name: LPL Financial Holdings, Inc.
reason: Strong advisor-recruiting growth (EPS CAGR 28%), but earnings depend on cash-sweep rates and market levels, and recent growth is acquisition-heavy (acq/FCF 1.39x).

name: Matador Resources Co.
reason: Oil and gas E&P whose earnings are set by commodity prices (margin 18-59%, FCF conversion -0.07).
